text:
New Jersey opens applications for $25 million rail freight assistance grants
A. M. Egan
The New Jersey Department of Transportation announced on Aug. 19 that it is accepting applications for $25 million in Rail Freight Assistance Program grants to fund projects aimed at improving the state's existing freight system and expanding service for businesses.
Grants will be distributed through a competitive process, focusing on projects that enhance port commerce connectivity, eliminate missing rail links to port facilities, upgrade trackage to a 286,000-pound load carrying capacity, and support a safe and efficient rail freight system. Owners or operators of short line railroads in New Jersey with an existing use and maintenance arrangement may apply for fiscal year 2027 grants through Oct. 9.
The program is administered by the Department of Transportation’s Division of Local Aid and provides funding for up to 90 percent of each project's estimated cost; sponsors are responsible for the remaining portion. Applications must be submitted through SAGE, the State’s online System for Administering Grants Electronically. All applicants are required to have an Eligibility Assessment Form approved within SAGE before submitting their application, with a limit of two applications per fiscal year.
According to the announcement, over the past five years more than $139.32 million has been invested in New Jersey's freight rail services using Transportation Trust Fund monies. This investment leveraged an additional $17.04 million from railroad owners and operators, bringing total investment close to $156.4 million.
For more information about the Rail Freight Assistance Program or other programs under the Division of Local Aid, individuals can visit njdotlocalhub.nj.gov.
The New Jersey Business and Industry Association serves as the nation's largest statewide employer association representing private-sector employers throughout New Jersey while advancing members' financial success through advocacy and partnerships among businesses, government entities, and academic institutions, according to the official website.
